channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Thai Baht: External cushion less generous – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Global Economics & Markets Research highlights that Thailand’s external buffers remain credible, but current-account dynamics have turned less favorable. Apr–May deficits reflect strong imports of energy and capital goods alongside resilient exports, reducing domestic value-added.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises as softer US jobs data weighs on the US Dollar
item.description: The NZD/USD pair advanced toward the 0.5700 level on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) weakened following softer-than-expected United States (US) employment data.

item.title: Pound Sterling holds the line, on loan from a cracking Dollar
item.description: The Pound bounced off the long-term support line that has repeatedly held near its seven-month lows, clawing back toward the cluster of moving averages overhead.

item.title: Japanese Yen bounces as Tokyo stops telegraphing its punches
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) rebounded from four-decade lows on Thursday, a move that owed nothing to the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: South Korean Won: Semiconductor risk and inflation dynamics – BNY
item.description: BNY’s report underscores heavy selling in South Korean semiconductor stocks and warns, via the OECD’s 2026 survey, that Korea’s reliance on chip exports heightens exposure to global tech-cycle swings.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: PMI resilience but trade risks grow – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao report that China’s private manufacturing PMI eased slightly to 51.7 but still delivered the strongest quarter in nearly six years, with official PMIs also beating expectations.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range bias holds near recent lows against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD closed at 1.2960 after a volatile session, with intraday swings between 1.2938 and 1.2975. For the coming day, he expects the pair to stay confined within a narrow 1.2935–1.2975 band.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Shooting star forms, bears eye 0.8000
item.description: The USD/CHF pair recoils on Thursday from a three-day high of 0.8120 after weaker-than-expected US data weighed on the Greenback, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) trading down 0.55%. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades at 0.8035, near ten-day lows.

item.title: Gold surges as weak US NFP knocks US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price soars over 2% on Thursday after the latest US employment report reduced the chances of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike and pushed the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields lower. The XAU/USD pair trades at $4,111 after bouncing off daily lows of $4,032.

item.title: USMCA: Prolonged negotiation cycle, not rupture – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish expects a drawn-out USMCA negotiation process rather than agreement expiry, highlighting comments from Mexican and US officials that downplay irreconcilable differences.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar weakens after softer US jobs data
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) came under pressure near the 100.90 level after the latest United States (US) employment report showed a clear slowdown in hiring. Nonfarm Payrolls rose by only 57,000 in June, while May’s gain was revised down to 129,000 from 172,000.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Bearish bias persists below 0.7000
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades on the front foot against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday as a weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report pushed back expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: Crude Oil forgets the war and shrugs at the tollbooth
item.description: Crude Oil finished Thursday at its lowest level in 18 weeks, which means the vast risk premium that built up around this year's conflict has fully bled away, back to pre-war levels.

item.title: United States Dollar Index retreats after US economy adds just 57K jobs in June
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades under pressure on Thursday as weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data dent expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average sets records while the chips fall
item.description: A June jobs report that undershot expectations by nearly half sent the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) to a fresh intraday record on Thursday, which reads like a contradiction until you look at what actually moved.

item.title: Asian FX: Scope for sharp rebound on US pressure – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that clients have largely capitulated on Japanese Yen (JPY) and South Korean Won (KRW) longs as these currencies stay weak versus US Dollar (USD) and Chinese Yuan (CNY).

item.title: Australian Dollar rises as weak US NFP weighs on the US Dollar
item.description: The AUD/USD pair climbed near the 0.6930 area on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) came under pressure following softer-than-expected United States (US) labor market data.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar advances as weaker US employment data weighs on US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD rises 0.59% on Thursday to trade around 0.5705 at the time of writing, supported by a sharp decline in the US Dollar (USD) following the release of a significantly weaker-than-expected US employment report.

item.title: British Pound rallies as weak NFP smashes Fed hike bets
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) registers solid gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after the latest US employment report missed estimates, reducing the chances of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: Germany: Reform drive supports growth narrative – ING
item.description: ING’s Carsten Brzeski analyses a new German government reform package focused on cutting red tape, increasing labour market flexibility, and capping healthcare and pension costs to restore competitiveness.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Weak NFP pushes XAG to the top of its weekly range
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) climbs to the top of its weekly trading range on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) slides to a two-week low after US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data surprised to the downside. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $61.15, up nearly 3.50% on the day.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Jobs slowdown supports steady rates – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Bernd Weidensteiner notes that weaker US employment data for June and downward revisions to prior months reduce pressure on the Federal Reserve to hike rates at the late-July meeting.

item.title: Indonesia: Stabilising FX and bonds as oil eases – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao notes that Indonesia’s onshore FX and bond markets have stabilised following a correction in global Oil prices, though gains are modest.

item.title: Japanese Yen rebounds on softer US payrolls, intervention risks
item.description: USD/JPY falls 0.92% on Thursday and trades around 161.05 at the time of writing after a much weaker-than-expected US employment report weighs on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Gold climbs as weak US NFP sends the US Dollar to a two-week low
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the front foot on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens amid rumors of a potential intervention by Tokyo after the Japanese Yen (JPY) hit a 40-year low earlier this week. The Greenback extended its losses following a weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: Euro hits nine-day high after softer-than-expected US NFP
item.description: The Euro (EUR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after weaker-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data reduced expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: BoE’s Mann: Activist move can bring inflation expectations and outcomes toward 2% target
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) policymaker Catherine Mann said on Thursday that an “activist move” may be needed if inflation expectations and outcomes move unfavorably, according to a speech text released by the BoE ahead of an event hosted by French bank Natixis.

item.title: Thailand: Narrow rebound, steady BoT rate – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Sathit Talaengsatya see Thailand’s 2Q26 starting stronger than feared, driven by exports and technology-linked investment, but with domestic demand still weak.

item.title: Central banks: Framework guidance shift reshapes analysis – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every highlights how Fed Chair Warsh and other major central bankers at Sintra are signalling a structural shift away from traditional forward guidance towards data-driven “framework guidance.” Every stresses that evolving AI, new inflation measures and reduced public tou

item.title: Mexico: USMCA review cycle extends uncertainty – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish argues that the US decision to opt for annual USMCA reviews instead of a 16-year extension prolongs policy uncertainty for Mexico while leaving near-term trade flows intact.
